answer: Each identity runs one canyon raven-watch post and locks a 65-credit bond. Each epoch it files a key-signed tally of raven flights, sealing it with a vine cord unique to that post. An auditor opens the box, recounts the dated slips, and checks the seal on the register; a missing slip, reused seal, or count mismatch burns the bond. The first post costs 29 credits, the k-th fake costs 29+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5024 and 1000 fakes cost 2,526,500 plus 65,000 at risk. A rented-post ring fails because slips are dated and bound to one key. An honest watcher pays 29 once and keeps the bond.
